status: The deploy is up and two of three goals are PROVEN, but the memory question is NOT settled - recorded honestly rather than declared fixed.

(2) realtime_events is FLAT under the flood: 4110 -> 4198 rows over 30 minutes, so message.part.delta really is no longer persisted. not_settled: RSS does NOT plateau. 20-minute window: 425MB (14:24) -> ~450MB (14:33) at ~3MB/min, then a STEP CHANGE at 14:34 to 647MB, then 732 / 1236 / 1345 / 1468 / 1591 / 1610 / 1707MB (14:41), a GC dip to 1379, 1797MB (14:43), a dip to 1058 (14:44).
reversal_the_unbounded_reading_is_not_es: Immediately after that window the live reading was VmRSS 335,940 kB (~328MB) with cgroup rss ~249MB - LOWER than the 425MB at 14:24. So a single GC reclaimed roughly 1.5GB, and the series is a LARGE-AMPLITUDE SAWTOOTH, not a monotonic climb. Two readings remain live: (a) BENIGN - with an 8Gi limit V8 sizes its heap much larger and collects lazily, so the sawtooth amplitude scales with the limit while the true retained set stays small; (b) MALIGNANT - the PEAK ENVELOPE is rising (419 -> 452 -> 647 -> 732 -> 1236 -> 1345 -> 1468 -> 1591 -> 1610 -> 1707 -> 1797MB) and some peak will eventually cross 8Gi. This is exactly why a 60-second sample interval is insufficient: it cannot see the envelope, and the envelope is what decides whether it OOMs.

leading_code_suspect: server/src/realtime/realtime.controller.ts:90 `const liveBuffer: RealtimeEvent[] = []`, :96 `liveBuffer.push(event)`, :118 iterating it - an UNBOUNDED array that accumulates every live event while the DB backlog is being read, with no visible backpressure handling. Because the delta frame deliberately still carries a FULL message snapshot (~1MB for a long message, measured 512KB text -> 1024.5KB frame) at ~35 deltas/s, a slow or absent consumer implies on the order of ~35 MB/s flowing into an unbounded array. This matches both the magnitude and the 14:34 step change.

trigger: User reported the frontend returning 500, then asked me to confirm whether the NFS storage class's host disk was full and whether MySQL caused it, and to clean up what could safely be cleaned.
CONFIRMED_YES: MySQL caused the space exhaustion. Evidence: the shared NFS volume (983.2G) was at 933.2G used / 0 available / 100%; MySQL's own data directory held 251 GB, of which 251.0 GB was 255 binary log files (~1 GB each, binlog.000001 from Sep 25 through binlog.000255). The mysql PVC CLAIMS only 20Gi, so the storage class enforces NO quota - the PVC had grown to 251 GB. Everything else in the vteam namespace totals ~2.5 GB (uploads 17.8M, worker-home 1.7G, worker-work 763M).
failure_chain: mysqld died with `[InnoDB] posix_fallocate(): Failed to preallocate data for file ./#innodb_temp/temp_5.ibt ... Operating system error number 28` (ENOSPC = 28) followed by `mysqld got signal 6` -> exitCode 2 -> CrashLoopBackOff, BackOff x11 over 87m. With the DB down, every request that touches it failed, so the app returned 500 (`prisma.worker.findUnique() ... Can't reach database server at vteam-mysql:3306`).
cleanup_performed: Deleted the 235 OLDEST binlogs (000001-000235) and kept the 20 newest (000236-000255) for recovery, rewriting `/data/binlog.index` to list exactly the surviving files (the index must stay consistent or mysqld refuses to start). Freed 233 GB: the NFS went from 933.2G used / 0 avail / 100% to 703G used / 231G avail / 76%, and the mysql PVC went from 251 GB to 22.5 GB. No other file was deleted - in particular nothing in `aiagents/`, and the other PVCs were only inspected, not modified.
recovery_verified: MySQL came up clean (1/1 Running, restartCount 0, 'ready for connections', no ENOSPC). Data intact: teams 7, agents 8, messages 2848, sessions 23, realtime_events 4262. The server needed NO restart: a direct Prisma query from inside the server pod returned DB_OK row=worker-37 (an earlier check of mine falsely looked like a DB failure but was actually my own script throwing on BigInt serialization), the last 30 seconds of logs were 200x8 / 201x3 / 202x204 / 405x1 with ZERO 500s, and /api/v1/health returned 200 {"status":"ok"}.
emergency_brake: SET PERSIST binlog_expire_logs_seconds=7200 (2 hours) - persisted to mysqld-auto.cnf, verified by reading it back. This bounds the steady-state binlog footprint to roughly 40-60 GB at the observed write rate. It is a brake, NOT a fix, and it should be relaxed once the write amplification is actually reduced.
ROOT_CAUSE_SHARED_WITH_THE_OOM_INCIDENT: The per-delta full-snapshot write. Every `message.part.delta` (~7-35/s) writes the FULL accumulated content to `messages`; with row-based binlogging that logs the whole row, producing ~20-30 GB/hour of binlog. The same write is what bloated `messages.ibd` to 3.57 GB for only 2848 rows (~1.25 MB/row). The earlier fixes stopped `realtime_events` persistence but never touched this write - which is why it is the last remaining amplifier.
NOT_OURS: After cleanup the NFS still shows 703G used while the entire vteam namespace accounts for only ~25 GB, so roughly 675 GB belongs to OTHER tenants on the same NFS host. The volume was already ~68% full before MySQL's 251 GB pushed it over. Reported to the user: cleaning our side cannot protect against other consumers, so the NFS host needs to be investigated.
remaining_actions: Lane dispatched to reduce the per-delta write amplification (throttle/coalesce the `messages` write, with guaranteed terminal flushes on task.completed, the D1 error path and the D2 watchdog path, and an explicit design against the mid-stream-MISS staleness hazard that throttling introduces).
`messages.ibd` (3.57 GB, ~1.25 MB/row) should be reclaimed with OPTIMIZE TABLE messages once convenient - it needs ~3.5 GB of temp space and 231 GB is now free.
The 2h binlog expiry should be relaxed after the write fix lands.
The NFS host's other ~675 GB of consumers are outside this namespace and must be looked at separately.

precedence_pitfall_found_and_fixed: The chart arg (3600) did NOT take effect at runtime: the live value stayed 7200 because SET PERSIST writes mysqld-auto.cnf and that OVERRIDES the command-line argument. question_answered: Where does MySQL's space go besides binlog, is it reasonable, and is there a cleanup strategy?
total: /var/lib/mysql = 22G, of which binlog is ~20G (91%) and EVERYTHING ELSE is only ~600MB.

breakdown.binlog: ~20G across 24 files - driven by the per-delta write amplification (~20GB/h). Bounded by the 1h expiry, but not reasonable in absolute terms.
breakdown.aiagents_tables: 223M total (measured from the .ibd files). realtime_events 120M for ~4.3k rows (~28KB/row), messages 75M for 2862 rows (~26KB/row), models 8M, tools 7M, triggers 7M, worker_model_availabilities 800K, workers 464K, sessions <425K, memories 416K. Reasonable for the design (message rows carry full content).
breakdown.ibtmp1: 13M but declared autoextend with NO upper bound - a latent disk-fill risk. Now capped at 2G via --innodb-temp-data-file-path=ibtmp1:12M:autoextend:max:2G (commit d09f40a); it takes effect on the next MySQL restart, so it will be applied together with the write-amplification deploy to avoid an extra outage.
breakdown.no_ddl_residue: No #sql-* / *.bak / *.old leftovers anywhere in the data directory.

cleanup_performed: ANALYZE TABLE on 8 tables (fixing the bogus statistics) and OPTIMIZE TABLE on 6 small bloated ones: workers 9MB->464KB (for a table with ONE row), worker_model_availabilities 12MB->800KB, models/tools/triggers each reclaimed 2-4MB. aiagents went 257M -> 223M.
MEASUREMENT_TRAP_CORRECTED: information_schema.tables reported realtime_events as 26,135.9MB / 347,420 rows. After ANALYZE it reports 109.5MB / 1,181 rows, while the actual .ibd file is 120MB. So the '26GB table' was a STALE ESTIMATE all along, and my earlier statements that the table had regrown to 26GB were WRONG. The disk-full diagnosis is unaffected because that was measured from the filesystem with du (255 binlog files = 251GB). Rule adopted going forward: judge table size only from the .ibd file or COUNT(*), never from information_schema.
verdict: Apart from binlog, MySQL's storage is entirely reasonable - the ~325MB of InnoDB system overhead is all config-bounded and the app data is 223MB.
open_decision: binlog is 91% of our footprint. Options presented to the user: (a) keep the 1h expiry (~20-30GB now, dropping to a few GB once the write amplification is fixed); (b) shorten the expiry to 15 minutes (~5GB, at the cost of a 15-minute PITR window); (c) disable binlog outright - there is no replica and no PITR practice here, so it would take the footprint to zero and also remove the per-row binlog cost from every write.

decision: Keep the binlog policy as-is (1h expiry, db.binlogExpireLogsSeconds=3600) and let the per-delta write-amplification fix bring the write rate down, rather than disabling binlog or shortening the expiry.
implication: Steady-state binlog footprint stays around 20-30GB until the write-amplification fix lands; after that it should fall to a few GB at the same 1h expiry. No further action required on binlog.
rationale: Minimal change: binlog stays available for point-in-time recovery, and the root cause (per-delta full-content writes generating ~20GB/h) is being fixed at the source rather than masked by a shorter retention window.
pending_application: The ibtmp1 cap (commit d09f40a, --innodb-temp-data-file-path=ibtmp1:12M:autoextend:max:2G) is declared in the chart but takes effect only on the next MySQL restart; it will be applied together with the write-amplification deploy so there is no extra outage.
